verdict.rationale: Dropbox's Dash surfaces AI-powered natural-language search, Q&A, summarization, and file organization ('AI answers for busy teams', 'organize files with AI', 'review documents with AI'), letting users interact via natural language for information tasks. However there's no evidence of natural-language commands driving core file operations (move, share, delete, sign) as an agentic interface — those remain menu/API-driven. Missing for 10: NL-driven execution of file/folder actions (not just search/summarize), evidence of a conversational agent that can act on commands, and independent corroboration of Dash's NL capability in practice.
